pages.name: Equals means level
pages.text: An [[equation]] says both sides are the same amount, like a balance sitting level. 8 + 4 = 7 + 5 is true, because both sides make 12.

pages.name: Fill the gap
pages.task: 8 + 4 = ? + 5. What number goes in the box, so both sides make the same amount?
pages.why: The left side makes 8 + 4 = 12. The right side already has 5, so the box needs 7, because 7 + 5 = 12.

pages.name: Same off both sides
pages.text: The box is the [[unknown]], x. Take 1 off one side only and it tips. Put it back, then take 7 off both sides and it stays level, leaving x = 5.

pages.name: Get x alone
pages.task: x + 3 = 10. Drag blocks off the pans until the box is alone, keeping the balance level.
pages.why: Each block off one pan needs one off the other to keep it level. With 3 off each, the box is alone and x = 7, and 7 + 3 = 10 checks it.

pages.name: Check it
pages.text: To [[check]] an answer, put it back in place of x. With 5 in the box, the left side makes 5 + 7 = 12, the same as the right.

pages.name: Check an answer
pages.task: Someone solves x + 6 = 15 and gets x = 21. Put 21 in place of x. What does the left side make?
pages.why: 21 + 6 = 27, which is not 15, so x = 21 fails the check. Taking 6 off both sides gives x = 9, and 9 + 6 = 15.

pages.name: Share both sides
pages.text: 4x means 4 lots of x. Share both sides into 4 equal parts and keep one, so divide both by 4. 36 ÷ 4 = 9, so x = 9.

pages.task: x + 4 = 11. Which move gets x alone and keeps the balance level?
pages.why: Taking 4 off both sides keeps it level and leaves x alone, so x = 7. As a check, 7 + 4 = 11.

pages.task: Put it together. Solve 21 = x + 13. What is x?
pages.why: Take 13 off both sides to leave x alone. 21 − 13 = 8, so 8 = x, which says x = 8. As a check, 21 = 8 + 13.
